questions.q_en:
Select the most appropriate collocation to substitute the underlined word in the given sentence.

The queen's palace is far away with my house.
questions.solution_en:
In the underlined part, the preposition 'with' which means 'accompanied by' is a contextually incorrect preposition as the word needs to indicate the distance of the palace from the point of reference (my house). Accordingly, option (c) 'away from' is the most appropriate option in which the preposition 'from' (indicating the distance between a particular place and another place used as a point of reference) is the ideal word to match the context of the given sentence.

Hence, the correct answer is option (c).

Note:

A Preposition is a word placed before a noun or a pronoun or a noun equivalent (pronoun, adverb, gerund, infinitive, adverbial clause, or any clause that can be used as the object of the preposition) and shows a relationship in space or time or a logical relationship between two or more people, places, or things in a sentence.

Examples

I. The teacher scolded the child for being late.

II. We're going to a party.

· The words in bold are called prepositions because they normally take position before (pre) a noun/pronoun or a noun equivalent (pronoun, adverb, gerund, infinitive, adverbial clause, or any clause that can be used as the object of the preposition.

· The noun/pronoun which is used with a preposition is called its Object.

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

The Federal Aviation Administration provides a psychiatrist to check a pilot's condition.
options_en: A psychiatrist will be provided by the Federal Aviation Administration to check a pilot's condition.
A psychiatrist is provided by the Federal Aviation Administration to check-in a pilot's condition.
A psychiatrist provided by the Federal Aviation Administration to check a pilot's condition.
A psychiatrist is provided by the Federal Aviation Administration to check a pilot's condition.
questions.solution_en:
The correct answer is option (d).

The subject of the Active Voice is changed into the object of the Passive Voice. Also, the object of the Active Voice is changed into the subject of the Passive Voice.

The usage of a 'to be' ['is' here] form of the verb is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Active to Passive.

The preposition "by" is used before the object made in Passive Voice. However, it is optional in some cases.

The Active voice in this question is in Present Indefinite. Thus, the Passive voice will also be in Present Indefinite.

The format of Active voice is: Subject + V1/ V5 + Object.

Thus, in Passive voice, the format will be: Object of the active voice (Subjective case) + am/is/are + V3 + by + Subject of the active voice (Objective case).

For example:

She likes you. (Active Voice)

You are liked by her. (Passive Voice)

The options except (d) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Passive Voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is: A psychiatrist is provided by the Federal Aviation Administration to check a pilot's condition.

Sentences of a paragraph are given below. While the first and the last sentences (S1 and S6) are in the correct order, the sentences in between are jumbled up. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

S1. In Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar

A. but also an elder statesman and national leader

B. we have not only a crusader against the caste system,

C. a valiant fighter for the cause of the downtrodden in India

D. whose contribution in the form of the Constitution of India

S6. will be cherished forever by posterity.
questions.solution_en:
Part B will come first as it mentions that in Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar, we get to see a crusader against a caste system. Part A follows and implies that not only a crusader but we can also see an elder statesman and a national leader in him. Part C further follows and mentions what all can be seen him. Part D preceded S6 and the pair D-S6 mentions that his contributions will be cherished forever.

The correct sentence is: In Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar, we have not only a crusader against the caste system, but also an elder statesman and national leader, a valiant fighter for the cause of the downtrodden in India, whose contribution in the form of the Constitution of India will be cherished forever by posterity.

So, the correct order is BACD.

Hence, option (c) is the answer.

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

Doctors saved many lives during the pandemic.
options_en: Many lives have been saved by doctors during the pandemic.
Many lives were being saved by doctors during the pandemic.
Many lives were saved by doctors during the pandemic.
Many lives are saved by doctors during the pandemic.
questions.solution_en:
To convert the active voice sentence "Doctors saved many lives during the pandemic" to passive voice:

The object "many lives" becomes the subject.

The verb "saved" (past simple) changes to "were saved" (past simple passive, as "lives" is plural).

The subject "doctors" becomes the agent, introduced by "by."

The sentence becomes: "Many lives were saved by doctors during the pandemic."

Checking the options:

Option 1: "Many lives have been saved" uses present perfect, which does not match the past simple tense.

Option 2: "Many lives were being saved" uses past continuous, implying an ongoing action, which is less appropriate.

Option 3: "Many lives were saved" correctly uses past simple passive.

Option 4: "Many lives are saved" uses present tense, which does not match the past context.

Thus, option 3 is the correct choice.

questions.q_en:
Select the grammatically correct sentence.

A. As a nation, India is a united country and shall always remain so.

B.As nation, India is a united country and shall always remain so.

C.As the nation, India is a united country and shall always remain so.

D.As a nation, India is an united country and shall always remain so.
questions.solution_en:
The grammatically correct sentence is A. This sentence is coherent and use the right articles. Sentence B is incorrect due to the omission of the article "a" before the noun "nation." It should be "As a nation" to indicate that India is being referred to as one of many nations. Without the article, the sentence lacks proper grammar. Sentence C is incorrect because it adds the definite article "the" before "nation". The use of "the" implies that there is a specific or particular nation being referred to, rather than India being considered as one among many nations. Using the definite article "the" before "nation" would not accurately convey the intended meaning of the sentence, which is to highlight India as a nation in general. Instead, the indefinite article "a" is more appropriate in this context to indicate that India is being considered as one among many nations. Sentence D is incorrect because of the use of the indefinite article "an" before "united country." The correct form should use "a" instead of "an." "A" is used before words that begin with a consonant sound, while "an" is used before words that begin with a vowel sound. In the given case, the word "united" starts with a consonant sound. Accordingly, article "a" should be used. Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

NOTE:

Definite and indefinite articles: In the English language, we have one definite article 'the'; it refers to or introduces, a particular, specific noun. 'An' and 'a' are indefinite articles; they refer to, or introduce, an unspecified noun.
